The test image shows a tomato leaf with:
- Extensive dark brown to nearly black necrosis covering most of the leaf
- Some remaining yellow-green areas interspersed
- Rough, blotchy texture
- No clear concentric rings or pinpoint spots
- No visible white/gray fuzzy spore masses

Top candidates: Late Blight (large dark water-soaked lesions), Gray Mold (dark blotchy necrosis), Leaf Mold (olive-green coloration). I'll use my reference view on Late Blight as the strongest candidate.

Comparing the reference Late Blight image to the test image:

**Reference Late Blight**: Shows brown necrotic areas with cleaner boundary against green tissue, papery/dry texture.

**Test image**: Much darker (almost black in places), more extensive damage covering nearly the entire leaf, olive-green areas mixed in with the dark necrosis, irregular blotchy pattern.

The test image is consistent with **Late Blight** at an advanced stage — the dark, extensive necrosis spreading across the leaf with remaining olive-green areas matches late blight progression under humid conditions. The very dark coloration aligns with "water-soaked, dark brown, and greasy" lesion description. The absence of visible white fuzzy sporulation could be because this is the upper leaf surface.
